Most eyelid bumps aren’t serious, but if you notice a lump that keeps coming back, changes, bleeds, affects your lashes, or makes it harder to move your eyelid, it’s time to get it checked. You can’t always tell what an eyelid lesion is just by looking, and similar-looking bumps can need very different care.

What Can Cause an Eyelid Bump?

An eyelid lesion can develop from a blocked gland, infection, cyst, skin growth, or tumor. A clinical review of benign eyelid lesions in NCBI Bookshelf lists common possibilities such as chalazia, papillomas, inclusion cysts, and other noncancerous growths.

Most lesions aren’t harmful. Where the bump is, how it’s growing, and your symptoms help decide if you need to watch it, treat it, remove it, or get a biopsy.

Which Eyelid Changes Should You Get Checked?

Plan to schedule an eyelid lesion evaluation if you notice any of these changes:

  • growth or a change in shape, size, or color
  • bleeding, crusting, an open sore, or a spot that won’t heal
  • missing eyelashes or distortion of the eyelid margin
  • a lump that keeps coming back in the same spot or makes it harder to blink or see

These signs don’t prove that a lesion is cancerous. A clinical review of malignant eyelid lesions explains that clinicians consider a growth’s timeline, rate of change, bleeding, lash loss, and recurrence when deciding whether biopsy is appropriate. Sudden vision changes, severe pain, fever, or rapidly spreading swelling need prompt medical care.

What Happens During an Eyelid Lesion Evaluation?

During your evaluation, the provider will check where the lesion is, what it looks like, how deep it goes, how it’s changed over time, and how it affects your eyelid. They’ll also look at your lashes, eyelid edge, eye surface, and the tissue around it.

When the diagnosis isn’t clear from the exam, a biopsy may be recommended. Depending on the lesion and its location, AestheticEye’s eyelid lesion removal services may include biopsy, removal, and reconstruction planning to preserve eyelid function and healthy tissue.

Why Does Oculoplastic Training Matter for Eyelid Lesion Removal?

Your eyelids are thin and flexible, protecting your eyes and helping you blink and move tears. If you need a growth removed near your lash line or eyelid edge, it takes careful work to protect healthy tissue and plan for reconstruction if needed.

Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament have completed advanced training in ophthalmology and oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery. If you’re in the Cincinnati-Dayton I-75 area, you can visit AestheticEye’s Cincinnati or Springboro offices to see specialists who look at both the lesion and the eyelid structure around it.

FAQ About Eyelid Bumps and Lesions

Is every eyelid lesion cancerous?
No. Most are benign, but you’ll need an exam to know for sure what your bump is.

Can a chalazion look like another eyelid lesion?
Yes. If you have a bump that keeps coming back or looks unusual, it’s a good idea to get it checked instead of trying home treatments over and over.

Does every eyelid bump need removal?
No. Treatment depends on what the bump is, your symptoms, where it is, and if it’s changing.

Will eyelid lesion removal leave a scar?
Any procedure can leave a scar, but how visible it is depends on the lesion, where it is, how it’s removed, how you heal, and if reconstruction is needed.

If your eyelid bump is changing, coming back, or making it harder to see, blink, or feel comfortable, AestheticEye can take a look and walk you through your options. Reach out to our Cincinnati or Springboro office to set up your appointment with an oculoplastic surgeon.
